# Review CHANGES REQUESTED for PAN-3941

# Review — PAN-3941
## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — shared focus restoration steals focus from successor dialogs

## Context
- Run ID: `agent-pan-3941-review-f157940a`
- Manifest: `/home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-3941/.pan/review/agent-pan-3941-review-f157940a/context.json`
- PR: `#3945` (`https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/pull/3945`)
- Branch / workspace: `feature/pan-3941` / `/home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-3941`
- HEAD reviewed: `f157940a983fd5fe5e56f9c31d5990d54ec7bbc2`
- Base / prior cycle SHA: `f702022974266dc6d16c1c637577dc4d3a7ce46e` / none
- Requirements source: GitHub issue `#3941`; the generated manifest's `acceptanceCriteria` array was empty.

## Blocking Findings

### [correctness / requirements] Menu cleanup steals focus from a replacement dialog — `src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/shared/ContextMenu.tsx:36`
- Severity: `!`
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect; `in_pr_scope`; violates the explicit requirement to preserve visible focus, keyboard navigation, and focus return.
- Trigger and changed-code connection: open a conversation action menu, then choose **Hand off to new conversation** or **Create summary fork**. The changed menu call sites set the fork target and close the menu in the same click (`ConversationPanel.tsx:862` and `:870`; equivalent paths exist in `ConversationActionMenu.tsx`). `ForkModal` mounts an input with native `autoFocus` at `ForkModal.tsx:316`, while the newly added `useReturnFocus` passive cleanup unconditionally calls `trigger.focus()` at `ContextMenu.tsx:42-43`.
- Expected / observed / impact: focus must remain inside the newly opened dialog. React applies native autofocus during the commit before passive effect cleanup, so the menu cleanup subsequently moves focus back to the old menu trigger behind the dialog. The modal opens visually, but keyboard input starts outside it.
- Evidence: static lifecycle trace across the changed `MenuSurface`, changed conversation-menu call sites, `useConversationMutations.openForkModal`, and the unchanged `ForkModal` autofocus target. This is also consistent with the external advisory in the manifest, but the finding was independently verified against HEAD. The existing tests only assert focus after a later dialog close and do not cover menu-to-dialog replacement.
- Fix: restore focus only when focus is genuinely lost (`document.activeElement` is `body`, `documentElement`, or `null`) or still belongs to the closing surface. Add a test that selects a menu action which mounts an autofocus dialog and asserts that the dialog field retains focus.

### [correctness / requirements] Right-click dismissal returns focus to the kebab instead of the invoking row — `src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/CommandDeck/ConversationRow.tsx:495`
- Severity: `!`
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect; `in_pr_scope`; violates the explicit focus-return requirement.
- Trigger and changed-code connection: right-click a conversation row, then dismiss the migrated menu with Escape or its backdrop. The right-click handler correctly focuses the row at `ConversationRow.tsx:287`, but the changed `MenuSurface` always receives `menuBtnRef`, which points to the kebab control at `:449`.
- Expected / observed / impact: a right-click-opened menu must return focus to the row that opened it; a kebab-opened menu must return focus to the kebab. Both paths currently return to the kebab, moving keyboard users to a different control and position.
- Evidence: direct static trace of both production open paths into the single `returnFocusRef`. The focused suite passes because `ConversationRow.test.tsx` has no menu-opening or focus-return coverage.
- Fix: track the actual opener for each path and pass that ref to `MenuSurface`. Add tests for both right-click and kebab invocation.

### [correctness / requirements] Radix disabled items lost their disabled styling — `src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/shared/ContextMenu.tsx:18`
- Severity: `!`
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect; `in_pr_scope`; violates the explicit requirement to preserve disabled/loading behavior.
- Trigger and changed-code connection: render a disabled issue action in a Radix context menu. The old wrappers included `data-[disabled]:pointer-events-none data-[disabled]:opacity-40`; the changed shared `MENU_ITEM_CLASS` contains only native `disabled:*` variants, while `ContextMenuItem`, `ContextMenuDestructiveItem`, and `ContextMenuSubTrigger` apply that class to Radix primitives at `:239`, `:254`, and `:287`.
- Expected / observed / impact: disabled actions must remain visibly disabled. Radix exposes this state as `data-disabled`, so the action remains behaviorally inert but now looks enabled, which makes unavailable actions misleading.
- Evidence: baseline-to-HEAD diff plus production wrapper trace. The new shared test covers native `MenuItemButton disabled`, not a disabled Radix item, so it does not catch this regression.
- Fix: restore `data-[disabled]:pointer-events-none data-[disabled]:opacity-40` in the shared class or each Radix wrapper, then test a disabled Radix item and sub-trigger.

## Non-blocking Findings

### [requirements / accessibility] Popup triggers do not consistently expose popup state — `src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/IssueActionMenu/IssueActionMenu.tsx:295`
- Severity: `~`
- Classification / requirement scope: validation gap; `whole_feature_scope`.
- Trigger and changed-code connection: the issue overflow trigger opens a role-menu without `aria-haspopup="menu"` or `aria-expanded`; the restart and system-control triggers open role-dialog popovers without `aria-haspopup="dialog"` (`CloisterStatusBar.tsx:383`, `SystemMenu.tsx:33`).
- Expected / observed / impact: screen readers should announce the popup kind and, for the menu trigger, its open state. The controls retain accessible names, so this is bounded rather than a blocker independent of the blocking focus defects.
- Evidence: static inspection of the changed shared-popup integrations and the current trigger markup.
- Fix: add `aria-haspopup` and the applicable `aria-expanded` state to each trigger.

### [correctness / UX] Escape from the Move submenu also closes its parent menu — `src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/CommandDeck/ConversationActionMenu.tsx:54`
- Severity: `~`
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect; `in_pr_scope`.
- Trigger and changed-code connection: open **Move**, then press Escape. The inner `MenuSurface` prevents the event and closes the submenu, but the existing window listener ignores `defaultPrevented` and closes the parent. `ConversationRow.tsx:135` has the same interaction.
- Expected / observed / impact: Escape should dismiss one menu layer at a time. Closing both is a bounded keyboard-navigation defect.
- Evidence: static event propagation trace through the changed nested `MenuSurface` and the production window listeners.
- Fix: have the window listeners return when `event.defaultPrevented` is true, and add a nested-menu Escape test.

### [review context] Stub-UI scanner findings are false positives — `src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/shared/ContextMenu.test.tsx:8`
- Severity: `?`
- Classification / requirement scope: unconfirmed hypothesis resolved as non-defect; `in_pr_scope`.
- Evidence: both `useState(false)` values are test-harness popup states with click handlers that set them to true. They are not exposed product stubs.

### Four dimensions
- Correctness / logic: completed across all 22 changed files and traced into unchanged `ForkModal`, `useConversationMutations`, dialog, and action-registry callers. Three blocking defects and one bounded nested-menu defect found.
- Security: no new trust boundary, HTML injection, dangerous URL construction, authorization change, dependency change, or sensitive-data handling was introduced. Existing fetch/action endpoints and confirmation gates are unchanged.
- Requirements / UX: semantic-color and shared-frame goals are substantially implemented, but focus return and disabled-state preservation are unmet. Popup semantics are incomplete. Visual acceptance and detector evidence remain unverified.
- Performance: no blocking I/O or unbounded work was added. Each open shared surface installs one resize listener and one `ResizeObserver`, both cleaned up on unmount; menu-item scans are bounded by the visible menu. The activity progress-bar change moves width animation to `transform`.

Reviewer reran 9 focused frontend files (72 tests) and Effect diagnostics. No Impeccable executable, report, or detector result was present. |

## Scope Note
The issue's six acceptance criteria were absent from the generated review manifest, so this review used the linked GitHub issue as the authoritative requirements source. Empty `chore: verify ...` commits and completed continuation flags were not treated as proof without an artifact or reproducible check. The Vercel Web Interface Guidelines review reinforced the popup-state advisories; it did not change the blocking verdict, which is based on the issue's own focus and disabled-state requirements.
